To view a copy of this license, visit http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/ We recently reported that circulating apolipoprotein AII (apoAII) isoforms apoAII-ATQ/AT (C-terminal truncations of the apoAII homo-dimer) decline significantly in pancreatic cancer and thus might serve as plasma biomarkers for the early detection of this disease. We report here the development of novel enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays (ELISAs) for measurement of apoAII-ATQ/AT and their clinical applicability for early detection of pancreatic cancer. Plasma and serum concentrations of apoAII-ATQ/AT were measured in three independent cohorts, which comprised healthy control subjects and patients with pancreatic cancer and gastroenterologic diseases (n = 1156). These cohorts included 151 cases of stage I/II pancreatic cancer. ApoAII-ATQ/AT not only distinguished the early stages of pancreatic cancer from healthy controls but also identified patients at high risk for pancreatic malignancy. AUC values of apoAII-ATQ/AT to detect early stage pancreatic cancer were higher than those of CA19–9 in all independent cohorts. ApoAII-ATQ/AT is a potential biomarker for screening patients for the early stage of pancreatic cancer and identifying patients at risk for pancreatic malignancy (161 words). Pancreatic cancer is one of the most lethal solid malignant tumors. To decrease the mortality of pancreatic cancer, efficient screening methods that will enable detection of the early stage of the disease and the identification of the precancerous lesions that are thought to be risk factors for pancreatic malignancy are needed 1 2 . Plasma/serum biomarkers for the early detection of pancreatic cancer would be useful clinical tools for screening patients in order to identify those who should undergo a second screening using stricter diagnostic modalities that can detect pancreatic dysfunction before imaging 3 . We recently reported the results of a mass spectrometry (MS)-based proteomic analysis, which showed that the levels of five circulating isoforms of apolipoprotein-AII (apoAII), including two novel isoforms, are significantly different in the plasma of patients with invasive ductal adenocarcinoma of the pancreas (IDACP) relative to healthy controls 4 5 . The five circulating apoAII-isoforms are characterized by the truncation of varying numbers of amino acids from the C-terminus of the apoAII homo-dimer. The isoforms were designated apoAII-ATQ/ATQ (apoAII-1, 17,380 Da) (the descriptions of -ATQ/ATQ etc. showed that each had the C-terminal sequence of an apo-AII isoform), apoAII-ATQ/AT (apoAII-2, 17,252 Da), apoAII-AT/AT (apoAII-3, 17,124 Da), apoAII-AT/A (apoAII-4, 17,023 Da), and apoAII-A/A (apoAII-5, 16,922 Da) ( Supplemental Figure 1 ) 5 . The circulating isoforms could be distinguished according to differences in molecular weight as determined by matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization-mass spectrometry (MALDI-MS) 5 . We previously reported the development of a novel and sophisticated MALDI-MS method for the semi-quantitative measurement of the levels of apoAII-isoforms in plasma. This MALDI-MS method was used to analyze more than 1,300 plasma/serum samples collected from patients at multiple medical institutions in Japan and Germany, in a previous study 5 . These analyses showed a statistically significant decrease in the level of apoAII-ATQ/AT in plasma and serum of IDACP patients compared with healthy controls from four independent cohorts 5 . These results suggested that apoAII-ATQ/AT would be good candidate plasma biomarkers for use in diagnosing early stage pancreatic cancer 5 6 , unlike other isoforms such as apoAII-ATQ/ATQ, -AT/AT, AT/A and A/A 5 . However, several factors impeded the clinical application of our MALDI-MS–based method for the measurement of apoAII-ATQ/AT. In this study, we developed novel sandwich ELISAs for the measurement of apoAII-isoforms in clinical samples. Our sandwich ELISAs provide for robust and rapid analysis of apoAII-isoforms. We evaluated the assays by measuring the plasma levels of apoAII-isoforms in samples from patients with pancreatic cancer and pancreatic disorders, including precancerous lesions and various malignant diseases of other organs, and we then compared the results with those of healthy controls. The Early Detection Research Network (EDRN), an initiative of the National Cancer Institute (NCI), is a consortium of institutions with the goal of accelerating the translation of biomarker information into clinical applications for the early detection of cancer ( http://edrn.nci.nih.gov ). The objectives of the EDRN include the development and testing of promising biomarkers or technologies for early detection of cancer and the evaluation of promising, analytically proven biomarkers or technologies. The EDRN has reference sets available for validating promising biomarkers for the early detection of cancer. The Japanese team applied for and received the pancreatic cancer reference set to validate the apoAII-isoforms biomarker for early detection of this cancer.

extracted_data.document_summary: This study focused on developing and validating novel enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays (ELISAs) for apolipoprotein AII (apoAII) isoforms, particularly the apoAII-ATQ/AT ratio, as diagnostic biomarkers for early-stage pancreatic cancer and for identifying individuals at high risk for pancreatic malignancy. The main findings indicate that apoAII-ATQ/AT levels significantly decline in pancreatic cancer patients, including early stages of invasive ductal adenocarcinoma of the pancreas (IDACP), showing superior diagnostic accuracy (AUC) compared to established markers like CA19-9 and DUPAN-2. The research also demonstrated that a combination of apoAII-ATQ/AT and CA19-9 further enhances diagnostic performance for early-stage pancreatic cancer by leveraging complementary aspects of disease pathology.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Diagnostic biomarker evaluation and assay development
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This study focused on the development and validation of novel sandwich ELISAs and, to a lesser extent, MS-based assays for quantifying apolipoprotein-AII (apoAII) isoforms. Plasma and serum samples were collected from various cohorts, including healthy controls and patients with pancreatic cancer (e.g., IDACP across stages), other pancreatic diseases, and gastroenterologic conditions. The analytical procedures involved specific sample preparation steps for MS (e.g., 50 µl plasma, desalting, elution, spotting) and dilution protocols for ELISAs (e.g., 1/5000 dilution for apoAII-AT/ATQ, absorbance at 450 nm). Diagnostic performance was assessed using AUC values, sensitivity, and specificity, with comparisons against established markers like CA19-9 and DUPAN-2. A linear logistic regression model was used for a combination biomarker. No therapeutic interventions or dose-response comparisons for treatment were performed or reported.

analyzed_biomarkers.activity_type: Ratio of protein levels (specific C-terminal truncated isoforms)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly lower in patients with pancreatic cancer (IDACP), including early stages, compared to healthy controls (e.g., P = 2.01 × 10−40 in cohort-1, P = 5.09 × 10−39 in cohort-2). Healthy controls (cohort-2) averaged 66.7 µg/ml, while IDACP patients averaged 36.6 µg/ml. Specifically, stage-I IDACP showed 38.8 µg/ml (P = 9.92 × 10−3 vs healthy). AUC values for distinguishing IDACP ranged from 0.935 (cohort-1) to 0.944 (cohort-2), and for early stage (I/II) IDACP were 0.941 (cohort-1) and 0.809 (95% CI, 0.748–0.867 for EDRN cohort). Significant decreases were also observed in various pancreatic diseases (e.g., IPMNs, chronic pancreatitis) and other gastroenterologic diseases, with AUC values up to 0.992. Substantially lower levels (<1.0 µg/ml) were observed in patients with IDACP, pancreatic diseases other than IDACP, cholangiocarcinoma, and duodenal carcinoma in some contexts.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: A specific ratio of C-terminal truncated apolipoprotein A-II (apoAII) isoforms. It reflects altered processing patterns of apoAII homodimers that are typically in homeostatic balance in healthy individuals, serving as a molecular indicator in pancreatic cancer and other pancreatic disorders.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Early-stage pancreatic cancer detection, including Invasive Ductal Adenocarcinoma of the Pancreas (IDACP) stages I/II. Also relevant for identifying patients at high risk for pancreatic malignancy and distinguishing IDACP from other pancreatic diseases (e.g., IPMNs, chronic pancreatitis, MCNs, SCNs) and various gastroenterologic diseases.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Highly accurate diagnostic biomarker for early-stage pancreatic cancer (IDACP) and for identifying individuals at high risk for pancreatic malignancy. It demonstrates superior diagnostic accuracy (AUC) compared to CA19-9 and DUPAN-2, making it useful for initial screening to identify patients requiring further diagnostic modalities. When combined with CA19-9, it achieves high sensitivity (95.4%) and specificity (98.3%) for detecting stage-I and stage-II IDACP.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly lower in IDACP patients compared with healthy controls (P = 1.14 × 10−18, AUC = 0.856 in cohort-1) and substantially lower levels (<1.0 µg/ml) in IDACP, other pancreatic diseases, cholangiocarcinoma, and duodenal carcinoma. The ELISA for apoAII-AT has higher affinity for apoAII/AT/AT than apoAII-ATQ/AT and apoAII-AT/A.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: An isoform of apolipoprotein A-II (apoAII), a component of high-density lipoprotein (HDL). It is a C-terminal modified homo-dimer involved in maintaining homeostatic balance of apoAII-isoforms.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: IDACP (various stages and cohorts), other pancreatic diseases, cholangiocarcinoma, and duodenal carcinoma, for early detection and risk factor assessment. Also used for evaluating ELISA assay specificity and as a surrogate marker.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: A potential biomarker for early detection of IDACP and identifying patients at high risk for pancreatic malignancy. The ELISA for apoAII-AT is considered a surrogate for apoAII-AT/AT levels, associated with IDACP diagnosis.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: variable; slightly higher in some IDACP contexts but substantially lower in others like IDACP, pancreatic diseases, cholangiocarcinoma, and duodenal carcinoma
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Slightly but significantly higher in IDACP patients compared to healthy controls (P = 0.0130, AUC = 0.427 in cohort-1) or substantially lower (<1.0 µg/ml) in IDACP, other pancreatic diseases, cholangiocarcinoma, and duodenal carcinoma. ELISA-ApoAII-ATQ showed high correlation (CC = 0.862) with MS-ApoAII-ATQ/ATQ.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: An isoform of apolipoprotein A-II (apoAII), a component of high-density lipoprotein (HDL). It is a C-terminal modified homo-dimer involved in maintaining homeostatic balance of apoAII-isoforms.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: IDACP (various stages and cohorts), other pancreatic diseases, cholangiocarcinoma, and duodenal carcinoma, for early detection and risk factor assessment. Also used for evaluating ELISA assay specificity and as a surrogate marker.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: A potential biomarker for early detection of IDACP and identifying patients at high risk for pancreatic malignancy. The ELISA for apoAII-ATQ is considered a surrogate for apoAII-ATQ/ATQ levels, associated with IDACP diagnosis.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Slightly but significantly lower in IDACP patients (mean 69.6 µg/ml) compared to healthy controls (mean 72.9 µg/ml). AUC = 0.666 for distinguishing IDACP (cohort-1). The reduction was slight, and AUC values were not sufficient for clinical usage.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Total apolipoprotein A-II (apoAII), a major protein component of high-density lipoprotein (HDL).
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasm (IDACP) and general pancreatic cancer, for biomarker evaluation compared to healthy controls. Measurement using a commercial APOA2 (human) ELISA kit.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Considered less effective and not sufficient for clinical usage as a biomarker for IDACP or general pancreatic cancer screening due to only a slight reduction in levels and insufficient AUC values (0.666).

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Higher in IDACP and related conditions, though often unchanged in early stages
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Statistically significant differences observed between healthy controls and IDACP patients (P = 1.58 × 10−13 in cohort-2). AUC for distinguishing IDACP (cohort-2) was 0.899, with stage-specific AUCs: stage-I (0.834), stage-II (0.952), stage-III (0.897), stage-IV (0.882). AUC for early stage (I/II) pancreatic cancer was 0.783 (95% CI, 0.699–0.855 for EDRN cohort). Elevated in acute benign biliary obstruction (p = 1.67 × 10−3). A cut-off of 75 units/ml was used in the study (typical clinical cut-off is 37 units/ml). Not overexpressed in the early stages of pancreatic cancer.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: A well-known tumor marker commonly used in the diagnosis and monitoring of pancreatic and other gastrointestinal cancers.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Diagnosis and monitoring of IDACP (all stages), other pancreatic diseases, acute benign biliary obstruction, and various other gastroenterologic cancers (cholangiocarcinoma, duodenal, hepatocellular, esophageal, gastric, colorectal carcinomas).
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: An established tumor marker for pancreatic cancer, but less effective for early-stage IDACP and not sensitive for general screening, especially in patients lacking the Lewis antigen. It has lower diagnostic accuracy than apoAII-ATQ/AT as a single biomarker for early detection and risk stratification. However, it can complement apoAII-ATQ/AT, significantly increasing the diagnostic accuracy (sensitivity 95.4%, specificity 98.3% for combination) for early-stage pancreatic cancer.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Implied to be elevated in IDACP, but less effective for early identification
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Statistically significant differences observed between healthy controls and IDACP patients (P = 4.96 × 10−25 in cohort-2). AUC for distinguishing IDACP (cohort-2) was 0.917, with stage-specific AUCs: stage-I (0.812), stage-II (0.850), stage-III (0.892), stage-IV (0.964). AUC values for distinguishing patients from healthy controls in other conditions ranged from 0.437 (SCNs) to 0.775 (MCNs). Did not identify patients at high risk for pancreatic cancer in the present study.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: A known tumor marker commonly used in the diagnosis and monitoring of pancreatic cancer.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Diagnosis and monitoring of IDACP (all stages) and various gastroenterologic diseases, particularly for evaluating its performance against other biomarkers in early-stage pancreatic cancer screening.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: An existing biomarker for pancreatic cancer, but consistently less effective for early-stage IDACP (e.g., stage-I AUC = 0.812) and identifying patients at high risk for pancreatic malignancy compared to apoAII-ATQ/AT.

analyzed_biomarkers.activity_type: Combined Biomarker Level (linear logistic regression model)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: AUC value was 0.879 (95% CI, 0.823–0.930). The improvement in AUC compared with the single biomarker CA19–9 was 0.0978 (95% CI, 0.040–0.169), which was statistically significant. The combination used log-transformed CA19–9 and apoAII-ATQ/AT in a linear logistic regression model: 12.065 + 0.503*log(CA19–9) – 3.403*log(ApoAII-ATQ/AT).

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Enhanced diagnostic performance by combining two different markers, potentially leveraging distinct aspects of pancreatic disease pathology.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Superior diagnostic accuracy for early detection of pancreatic cancer compared to individual biomarkers CA19-9 or apoAII-ATQ/AT alone.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Elevated in patients with IDACP in comparison with non–pancreatic disease patients. The AUC for distinguishing pancreatic cancer from non-pancreatic disease was significantly lower than the AUC for CA19–9.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: An exopeptidase that cleaves amino acids from the C-terminus of a protein or peptide, primarily synthesized by the pancreas.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Potential indicator for IDACP, but with lower diagnostic accuracy compared to CA19-9. Its elevated activity might explain the apoAII isoform hyper-processing phenotype in pancreatic disorders but not the hypo-processing phenotype.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: ELISA-ApoAII-ATQ showed high correlation (CC = 0.862) with MS-ApoAII-ATQ/ATQ; ELISA-ApoAII-ATQ has higher affinity for ApoAII-ATQ/ATQ than ApoAII-ATQ/AT.

analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Measurement for understanding ELISA assay specificity and as a surrogate marker.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: ELISA-ApoAII-ATQ is considered a surrogate biomarker for the amount of apoAII-ATQ/ATQ.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: ELISA-ApoAII-AT has a higher affinity for apoAII/AT/AT than apoAII-ATQ/AT and apoAII-AT/A.

analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Measurement for understanding ELISA assay specificity and as a surrogate marker.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: ELISA-ApoAII-AT is considered a surrogate biomarker for apoAII-AT/AT.
